title: docs: "key must be not be" → "key must not be"
description:
The error message in `key_from_sexp()` ([`src/fastmap.cpp`, line 24](https://github.com/r-lib/fastmap/blob/main/src/fastmap.cpp#L24)) has a typo:

```
key must be not be "" or NA
```

Should be:

```
key must not be "" or NA
```

### Reprex

```r
library(fastmap)
m <- fastmap()
m$set("", "value")
#> Error in m$set("", "value") : key must be not be "" or NA
```

title: Use a hash map library that has consistent ordering across platforms
description: See https://github.com/r-lib/fastmap/issues/8#issuecomment-497942394. The idea is that the order from `$keys()` and `$as_list()` doesn't have to be sorted in any particular fashion; it just should be consistent across platforms so that users aren't surprised when behavior isn't reproducible when moving code from one platform to another.

title: Serializing and deserializing fastmap with no holes doesn't work right
description:
A new `fastmap` filled with exactly 32 items will have no holes. When serialized and unserialized, the resulting object provides the wrong result for `as_list()`:

```R
x <- seq_len(32)
m <- fastmap()
m$mset(.list = setNames(x, as.character(x)))
m1 <- unserialize(serialize(m, NULL))

m1$as_list()
#> named list()
```

This is because of this line:

https://github.com/r-lib/fastmap/blob/1d7890cd1ad1c665073671537e8f306ef4fa52de/R/fastmap.R#L435

This line is supposed to remove the original vector with `n_holes` items removed. However, when `n_holes` is 0, then `holes` is a length-0 vector, and `x[-integer(0)]` will return an empty vector instead of what we want, which is just the original `x` unchanged.

title: Exceptions for missing keys?
description:
Currently, fastmap allows returning `NULL` or some other value specified by `missing` or `missing_default`. The sentinel value `missing_key()` is one possible value to return.

In some cases, it may be useful to throw an exception when trying to fetch a key that is missing. One possibility is to allow the user to pass a function to `missing` or `missing_default`, like so:

```R
m <- fastmap(missing_default = function(key) stop("Key '", key, "' is missing", call. = F))

m$get("foo")
#> Error: Key 'foo' is missing
```

An alternative is to simply leave things as is, and have the user call `m$exists()` (and possibly throw) before calling `m$get()`.

title: Consider switching back to `std::map`
description:
fastmap currently uses `std::unordered_map`. Because of this, if you call `m$keys()` or `m$as_list()`, the order is arbitrary and can differ across platforms. This means that code that behaves one way on one computer can behave a different way on another computer. In Shiny, for example, this means that reactives might fire in different orders on different computers: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/2466#issuecomment-497904851

With environments, the order is arbitrary, but at least it is consistent across platforms.

We should consider replacing the `std::unordered_map` with either `std::map`, or some other implementation that behaves consistently across platforms.
